elements.element: Renewal must occur either (i) only by mutual written agreement or (ii) automatically in 12-month renewal periods.
elements.evidence: The clause uses the permitted automatic-renewal mechanism and renews for successive one-year periods on each anniversary.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer may opt out on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The Company, treated as Customer, may terminate on 30 days' written notice. Although framed as termination rather than expressly as non-renewal, this right is broad enough to prevent an upcoming renewal.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must give Customer a reminder 60 days before each renewal.
elements.evidence: HDI must notify the Company in writing of each upcoming automatic renewal not less than 60 days before the applicable anniversary.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no renewal price-increase cap, and the absence of a right to increase prices is not demonstrable from the provided language.
The agreement automatically renews on each anniversary.

elements.element: Customer's non-renewal notice window must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The Company, treated as Customer, has a 30-day written-notice period. HDI's separate 90-day period does not enlarge Customer's notice burden.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at 5% or less.
elements.evidence: No price-increase cap appears in the operative language.

result.reason: The redline implements 12-month automatic renewals, a 30-day Customer exit right, and a 60-day Vendor reminder, but omits every renewal price cap. It therefore satisfies neither complete position. The changes are targeted and preserve unrelated terms, but the clause is incomplete and its punctuation and use of general termination language rather than explicit non-renewal language reduce drafting precision.
